scope: Proposed acceptance obligations, not executable tests or runtime results. Existing tests are reviewed starting points and may need extension. Select cases by touched seam; do not require every case for every PR.
execution_receipt_requirements: Exact source and dirty/generated state, actual fixture implementation and case roster, baseline/candidate identities
Engine version/hash, OS/architecture, real backend/library or explicit not applicable, profile and route identities
Actual stimulus/event/poll/tick trace as applicable, independent expected result and observed result
Checked process verdict, expected terminal summary/count, exit status, complete collection, engine/script diagnostics and warning disposition
Receipt path/hash and PASS, FAIL or INCOMPLETE verdict; hardware/build/display/transport identity for physical claims
A new dated result record for execution; this historical audit remains UNRUN

organization_refinement.scope: Source and primary-research refinement; all runtime case executions remain UNRUN.

cases.title: Stale connection cannot authorize resume
cases.when: Selection, status, intent dispatch or resume ownership changes.
cases.trigger: Capture ready status, then disconnect/reconnect or reuse the selected numeric handle before the next poll and actual Continue dispatch. Distinguish supported role/connection callbacks from artificial field mutation.
cases.oracle: The owner revalidates the current connection/generation and full family gate. Stale evidence grants no accepted tick/action. Existing guarded recovery remains available; no adapter cache supplies authority.
cases.evidence: Observed live role/generation, input owner, dispatch order and first accepted command/tick; displayed status alone is not fresh admission.

cases.title: Relevant profile change invalidates stale permission
cases.when: Profile activation, readiness projection or queued intents change.
cases.trigger: Capture status, then successfully activate a relevant mapping/action/calibration or role before Continue and the next poll. Separately inject prepublication failure, activation refusal, complete restoration and failed/unobserved restoration in both managed save paths; identify any direct-mutation-only fixture.
cases.oracle: Dispatch validates the actual accepted source/profile and applicable readiness. A successful relevant change cannot reuse stale evidence. A false Save does not prove unchanged storage/runtime/roles: observe each phase and preserve the existing distinction; an explicit recovery repair holds uncertain authority until re-admitted. Harmless fields need not invalidate unrelated state.
cases.evidence: Accepted and stored profile identities, actual restoration results, UI feedback, holds and first command; no blanket rollback or newly invented global revision.

cases.title: Retired activity rejects late work
cases.when: Bridge listeners, async/deferred work or activity replacement changes.
cases.trigger: Queue an origin-bound status/pause/resume/profile/load request for activity A; replace it with B before delivery. Separately change source on the same activity before a scheduled reconciliation, and detach/reattach the same original Workshop pause/session. Include the old deferred refresh callback if its guard is changed.
cases.oracle: Retired A cannot act on B or clear B's listeners/recorders. Current-activity reconciliation may legitimately rebind/hold the latest source without borrowing old authority. Temporary Workshop suspension returns unavailable while detached and can restore the same provider on reattachment; it is not final disposal. A new provider guard alone does not prove the rest of deferred refresh is safe.
cases.evidence: Activity identity, queued/completed operation order, listener counts and actual state/recording outcomes; extend beyond existing fixtures where absent.

cases.title: Independent holds and explicit player intent
cases.when: Pause/resume or launch/restart consumers move.
cases.trigger: Combine menu with controller-loss/calibration/fault holds; clear only the menu hold. Separately run ready Home Fly and guarded restart through their current shell routes.
cases.oracle: Remaining holds prevent unauthorized progress and expose their recovery reason. Preserve owner ordering and existing Fly/restart intent; do not force an extra Continue on already-admitted launch or auto-resume after loss.
cases.evidence: Active hold set, shell screen identity, operation result and first tick; test actual shell plus session.

cases.title: Verified gamepad readiness stays immediate
cases.when: Trusted connection, polling or readiness changes.
cases.trigger: Use a verified standard gamepad fixture and its first valid trusted poll without prior motion/neutral dwell. Compare a distinct unverified/raw fixture and applicable managed/direct routes.
cases.oracle: Verified pad readiness retains its existing first-valid-poll behavior without new dwell or motion gesture; invalid/unverified evidence is not elevated. Continue/launch admission still follows the owning activity.
cases.evidence: Fixture trust identity, poll/readiness trace and actual gate; do not generalize raw-fixture neutral-dwell tests.

cases.title: Radio evidence survives correct temporal boundaries
cases.when: Radio polling, action edges, focus/reconnect or verification integration changes.
cases.trigger: Hold ON or throttle raised before selection/reconnect/focus recovery; inject ordinary polled zeros, unrelated events, then the applicable real LOW/OFF/center evidence. Separately exercise a completed same-generation verification challenge seed.
cases.oracle: Ordinary unverified polls do not fabricate required recovery evidence; edge actions need the owning OFF/ON policy. Preserve the trusted finite center/OFF verification seed and separate raw-radio LOW evidence.
cases.evidence: Event/poll origin, generation, verification proof, edge transitions and first accepted command, including near-threshold jitter.

cases.title: Held menu keys cannot become flight axes
cases.when: Keyboard polling, pause exit or held-key masks move.
cases.trigger: Select Continue with Down still physically held; observe first flight poll/tick, then release and press again. Hold an independent second axis and compare positional radio sticks.
cases.oracle: Down cannot become pitch until its owning per-axis mask sees release; a new press works. Other axes retain independent mask behavior and radio positional inputs are not keyboard-masked.
cases.evidence: Actual shell close-pause ordering, global key poll, masked command and first accepted tick; event consumption alone is insufficient.

cases.title: Capture owns binding and release
cases.when: Capture, selected-device leases or focus handoff changes.
cases.trigger: Capture an assigned Pause/Back using the selected controller or supported keyboard; send a foreign-controller event and the matching release; cancel or lose the connection while the draft is dirty.
cases.oracle: Supported keyboard/selected-device capture works; foreign devices cannot bind. Matching release cannot escape into navigation/flight. Cancellation/loss restores the documented focus/draft state without silently saving or discarding unrelated edits.
cases.evidence: Capture owner, selected generation, draft before/after, consumed release and absence of unintended activity action.

cases.title: Text input and action edges remain separate
cases.when: Keyboard shortcuts, text focus or action dispatch moves.
cases.trigger: Type a remapped Back chord in an editable field, exercise explicit Escape, repeat keydown and simultaneous modifier release, then perform the same shortcut outside text/capture.
cases.oracle: Typing is not navigation or flight action; documented Escape recovery remains. Edge actions dispatch once under the actual chord/repeat policy and work in their supported non-text context.
cases.evidence: Focused widget, consumed events, action count and visible recovery; fixed keyboard axes do not imply full keyboard remapping.

cases.title: Admitted quad Pause reaches the real consumer
cases.when: Quad or shared action admission/dispatch changes.
cases.trigger: For each retained supported radio button, learned-axis or custom-key Pause form, validate and save/activate, then exercise applicable OFF/press/release through the real activity; otherwise verify explicit refusal/disable before Save. Retest P/Escape and the existing pad route.
cases.oracle: Every presented supported form actually pauses; otherwise assignment is refused before misleading success. Foreign/stale sources and held/repeat events cannot trigger extra actions. Resume retains quad readiness and arm/rate policy.
cases.evidence: Setup-to-activity integration witness with selected binding, action count and session pause; input/plant-only fixtures are insufficient.

cases.title: Airship native menu map follows the UI role
cases.when: Airship menu/role mapping or shared native mapping changes.
cases.trigger: Lose UI role, reuse its old handle without selecting it and verify clearing; then select a different handle, change eligibility/binding and select keyboard-only. Separately intentionally select an eligible reused handle. Exercise the real callback chain.
cases.oracle: Unselected reused-handle events cannot use a stale map; when a different handle is selected only that role's map matches. Intentional selection of the reused handle rebuilds its current eligible role/profile mapping and works. InputMap matching alone cannot distinguish physical generations sharing one number. Flight role stays unchanged; qualify focusable HUD separately.
cases.evidence: InputMap before/after and actual native HUD focus/action; physical reused-device behavior is a separate row.

cases.title: Uncached airship profile refusal can recover explicitly
cases.when: Airship resume/profile resolution or shared recovery changes.
cases.trigger: Hold the V2 store lease from another instance before fresh uncached selected connection; refuse lookup, release contention, then choose Continue on the same connection. Also retain busy/corrupt/ambiguous and stale-selection variants.
cases.oracle: Release alone never resumes. Explicit recovery re-resolves current ownership and proceeds only through live armed/low-throttle/centered-yaw gates. Repeated refusal stays held with reachable recovery; a cached success remains distinct.
cases.evidence: Lease, resolver call, current generation/profile, actual Continue gate and HUD outcome. Do not invent an airship Controls button.

cases.title: Legacy concurrent saves retain acknowledged updates
cases.when: Legacy calibration/smoke writer, caller or storage transaction moves.
cases.trigger: Two processes load the same seeded legacy file; schedule competing different-device, same-device and calibration-versus-smoke writes using a barrier only in an identified disposable source copy.
cases.oracle: After repair, acknowledged updates survive under the documented merge policy or explicit contention/retry is returned. Unrelated sections remain. Failed publication does not falsely acknowledge success; V2 concurrency remains separately intact.
cases.evidence: Process schedule/instrumentation hashes, responses and unmodified-reader results. Existing V2 concurrency tests alone do not cover legacy; no power-loss durability claim.

cases.title: Every admitted range has truthful endpoints
cases.when: Profile validation, normalization, import or readiness changes.
cases.trigger: Use external absolute and signed profiles below/at/above the chosen minimum-span contract, including 5e-7 historical witness, off-center sides and inversion; save/reload/import and poll real readers.
cases.oracle: Endpoints produce documented finite full/idle commands or activation refuses with a field-specific error. No admitted misleading idle/readiness. Ordinary calibrated profiles and recoverable files remain intact; tiny wizard-unreachable inputs are not generalized to all pilots.
cases.evidence: Exact profile bytes, admitted/refused result, endpoint outputs and distinct gamepad/radio LOW behavior.

cases.title: Shaping, rates and trims keep their order
cases.when: Conditioning, preview data, rate selection or tick input changes.
cases.trigger: Use declared nonzero raw samples and independently computed expected values for Mode 1/2, offset/inverted calibration, transmitter versus simulator rates, pad expo, airplane normal/sport rates and retained trims. Include absolute-trigger endpoints and both triggers.
cases.oracle: Each stage applies its owned transform exactly as characterized; no double expo or lost trim. Preview describes its actual stage, absolute throttle retains direct normalization and hold paths do not integrate rate throttle. Do not impose airplane curves on quad.
cases.evidence: Raw/profile/conditioned/session/accepted-command values, justified numerical tolerance and stage labels; add actual consumer witness if absent.

cases.title: Quad frame sampling and curve ownership stay distinct
cases.when: Shared input sampling or quad adapter/FC boundary changes.
cases.trigger: Feed identical pre-expo pilot frames through the real quad path, including stages within one tick and held/recovery intervals; compare accepted FC state/input before and after extraction.
cases.oracle: FC sample remains once per tick under the existing framed-sampled protocol; stage evaluation does not resample or reapply airplane shaping. Checkpointed controller memory and accepted commands remain identical where guaranteed.
cases.evidence: Pilot frame, sampling count, stage calls, accepted memory and checkpoint identity; actual backend scope stated.

cases.title: Quad fallback remains held with correct recovery
cases.when: Quad source selection, focus recovery or Continue changes.
cases.trigger: Compare ordinary same-source pause with focus/source loss while another controller, including radio/unknown kind, remains connected. Observe automatic fallback, paused stored motor state, Continue and first resumed tick.
cases.oracle: Fallback does not auto-resume and invalidates arm continuity. Preserve ordinary frozen rate throttle versus source/focus recovery reset/disarm. Identify the replacement source before Continue as an explicit owner-qualified GCA-G3 acceptance; do not silently change paused stored-frame semantics.
cases.evidence: Selected source/generation, display, pause/arm state before and after first tick; any UI/policy repair is separate behavior work.

cases.title: AUX no-command preserves owned targets
cases.when: AUX sampling, hold/rearm or command reuse changes.
cases.trigger: Set bound flap/gear targets, enter menu/focus/source holds, poll unarmed axis/button bindings, then send applicable fresh OFF and ON. Include smoke separately.
cases.oracle: Unarmed bound AUX is no command, not zero/retract. Existing flap/gear targets and actuator continuity remain; smoke follows its separate off-at-boundary policy. Rearming cannot invent an extra edge.
cases.evidence: Validity flags, requested targets, accepted inputs and actuator state with axis/button variants.

cases.title: Hold sampling does not drift virtual throttle
cases.when: Polling, virtual throttle or pause/resume ordering changes.
cases.trigger: Where the family has rate throttle, hold a nonzero rate stick through ordinary pause and repeated nonintegrating samples, then resume through the proper owner; separately test refused/faulted tick boundaries.
cases.oracle: The held value follows the existing family policy without menu drift or duplicate integration. Characterize pre-tick input accumulator behavior under refusal/fault; do not invent universal rollback with physical state.
cases.evidence: Accumulator and sample sequence, integrate flag, hold value and first accepted command; preserved family exceptions named.

cases.title: Invalid samples fail through the owning safety gate
cases.when: Validation, sampling reuse or controller readiness changes.
cases.trigger: Inject NaN/Inf, an absent or invalid reader callable, invalid profile axis indices and known ownership loss; include held unbound buttons where they affect existing edge readiness. Distinguish these observable failures from a physically absent axis reported as zero.
cases.oracle: Failures exposed by the validated reader/profile contract cannot become trusted readiness or retain stale authority. Preserve the family's fail-safe/hold and bounds/finite validation across cached/live paths. Do not invent missing-channel detection where the API returns ordinary zero; hardware counts/trigger independence remain separately qualified.
cases.evidence: Injected sample/profile bytes, rejection reason, current readiness and accepted-command absence or documented safe fallback.

cases.title: Save and activation report the route's true result
cases.when: Setup Save/apply, calibration completion or persistence callbacks move.
cases.trigger: Inject managed preflight/publication/activation failure, then separately fail disk, role or runtime restoration in full Controls Save and in-flight calibration/smoke where the route attempts that component; otherwise record not attempted/not applicable. Include successful publication with cleanup warning and keyboard/unassociated/no-session saves. Separately fail direct legacy calibration/smoke after in-memory activation; characterize duplicate-device arrival during direct smoke assignment.
cases.oracle: Distinguish unchanged, published, applied, restored and unknown component outcomes. Managed compensation is attempted, not guaranteed; do not infer unchanged state from false. The proposed recovery repair retains draft/recoverable data and keeps uncertain authority held until re-admission, with truthful real-caller copy. Saved is separate from applied, which may be not requested/not applicable. Cleanup warning is not failed publication. Direct legacy can remain active but NOT saved until an explicit behavior repair changes it.
cases.evidence: Before/after primary/rollback files, active profile, roles/holds, returned component states, actual Controls/HUD copy, draft and restart. A mocked false result alone does not exercise compensation.

cases.title: Storage interruption does not invent defaults or success
cases.when: Store admission/publication/locking or migration changes.
cases.trigger: Use isolated files and controlled schedules for corrupt/missing/recovered storage, write/restore refusal and interrupted leases. Two editors load profile P, A edits axes and saves, B edits an old name and saves later; repeat via managed calibration/smoke. Include different UUIDs, changed durable menu preference, shared association, concurrent legacy imports and an L1-derived new V2 draft after legacy L2 is saved.
cases.oracle: A valid V2 rollback copy retains recovery provenance; otherwise unreadable storage remains an error. Legacy writers do not overwrite unreadable input; legacy empty-reader ambiguity is separately characterized. Proposed stale-edit repair compares actual stored bases, not UI dirty fingerprints. Full setup reviews a changed durable menu base; narrow writers preserve it without adopting another process's role. Different UUIDs may share association dependencies; legacy origin needs coordination or a supported coexistence restriction. Preserve conflicting drafts and acknowledged data; no silent semantic merge, automatic stale-lock deletion, unbounded tick-path retry or unproved power-loss claim.
cases.evidence: Source/barrier identity and schedule; canonical base/current/candidate profiles including association, menu preference, legacy origin, returned outcomes, runtime role, file/lock state and restart. Distinguish current source-inferred last-writer behavior from proposed conflict-refusal acceptance.

cases.title: Restart and rollback retain usable player profiles
cases.when: Profile compatibility, default interpretation or release rollback is affected.
cases.trigger: Use copies of accepted V2/legacy files and menu preference, including gamepad-only smoke, partial/unreadable legacy import, ambiguous/reused identities and stale legacy-origin drafts. Save supported edits, restart candidate, then reopen retained baseline. Characterize old readers with open handles/missing-path windows and noncooperating old writers, or declare unsupported coexistence.
cases.oracle: Structural changes preserve schema and declared selection semantics. Candidate migration preserves every supported radio/AUX/action and separate gamepad-smoke value or explicitly reports unsupported conversion; surface read/skip errors without changing original legacy bytes. No persisted numeric handle or UUID proves physical identity. Explicit flight selection remains session-local unless separately designed; HUD stick mode is not keyboard remapping. Old/new data and concurrent-version policy need actual proof; source revert alone is insufficient.
cases.evidence: Build/profile bytes, launch logs, selected roles and recovered user-visible settings; original player files remain protected.

cases.title: Managed, direct and trial routes remain explicit
cases.when: A launch route or common service dependency changes.
cases.trigger: Inventory and execute affected Home, AppRoot direct, standalone/component and Workshop routes with declared keyboard/verified-pad/radio fixtures. Distinguish direct quad's self-created V2 service from its no-registry legacy fallback; include temporary Workshop menu/session restoration and actual offered action/binding-form rows.
cases.oracle: No mandatory service breaks an intentional service-free route. Home preferences and direct legacy/profile behavior retain their declared scope. Unsupported menu/binding combinations are labeled before use, not inferred from another activity's pass.
cases.evidence: Actual launch flags/catalog/route, services and resolver, saved versus current-run preferences, action/form consumer or exclusion, and first accepted command. Use organization-map.json and action-consumers.json as source starting points, not support receipts.

cases.title: First post-gap tick is observed before policy changes
cases.when: Scheduling or gap/focus/recovery behavior moves; not an unrelated status projection.
cases.trigger: Use an injected monotonic clock at the actual activity tick boundary to model a long application processing gap without focus/disconnect events; compare steady-input sparse events and a normal cadence.
cases.oracle: Record whether any stale command is accepted before hold detection, then choose and test an explicit family-owned policy if needed. Do not claim a confirmed native sleep defect, infer loss from stationary axes or attach incompatible sessions just to reuse a watchdog.
cases.evidence: Clock/tick/admission trace and current behavior classification; any changed policy requires a separate repaired oracle and native suspend qualification.

cases.title: RF loss and USB removal are qualified separately
cases.when: A physical radio or wireless route is claimed supported, or its recovery changes.
cases.trigger: On identified hardware, select separate applicable subcases: USB unplug, Bluetooth power/sleep, and transmitter-off with a separately enumerated receiver. A USB-only radio need not have an RF receiver in its input path; record inapplicable subcases.
cases.oracle: Record observed input/failsafe behavior per applicable transport. No unchanged-axis/RF-health inference or synthetic USB result qualifies transmitter loss. Inapplicable and unobservable RF status remain distinct from a pass or failure.
cases.evidence: Exact device/firmware/OS/transport/build, report/video and observed recovery; no hardware test was performed by this audit.

cases.title: Fixed-wing refusal and committed faults remain distinct
cases.when: Reset/restore/reload/observer transaction moves, not merely a status view.
cases.trigger: Inject candidate refusal before commit, then observer fault/reentry after a separately accepted reset or restore. Record old/new flight, writer and statistics identities.
cases.oracle: Precommit refusal preserves old accepted frame/writer with no publication. Postcommit fault leaves the accepted frame paused, emits the owner-specified outcome once and closes the correct old footer; restore remains noncredit. Do not retry a committed reset as if rolled back.
cases.evidence: Commit receipts, exact frame/inputs, callback sequence, old footer/ticks and correct statistics-generation or noncredit result.

cases.title: Other families do not inherit a false reset guarantee
cases.when: Airship/quad reset or recorder publication is explicitly included in a later slice.
cases.trigger: Inject airship reset rejection after resetting notification and quad context-changing reset observer/failed retry; observe recorder state and accepted physical frame at every boundary.
cases.oracle: Characterize actual ordering before extraction. Current early recorder notification is not called fixed-wing-style rollback. Preserve current behavior in structural work, or define and prove a separately owned preservation repair; no lost-byte incident is assumed from source alone.
cases.evidence: Fault-injection timeline, recorder/footer/completeness and state; scope remains outside the first pause/resume bridge.

cases.title: Exit and tentative detach preserve owned data
cases.when: Replacement, recording finalization, export, disposal or worker lifetime moves.
cases.trigger: Cancel/fail replacement after tentative detach; repeat close/cancel; inject writer/export failure and pending race results; deliver late loader completion. Exercise explicit discard only through the existing owner choice.
cases.oracle: Tentative detach does not finalize the surviving flight. Report publication/export failure and preserve/recover data where the owning contract guarantees it; label incomplete or unrecoverable output truthfully. No automatic discard, wrong-owner close, duplicate callback or live-worker join that blocks required main-thread work.
cases.evidence: Owner identities, replacement result, file/sample/outbox state and retirement order; no universal close API required.

cases.title: Detached status is truthful and cannot mutate authority
cases.when: Status projection, operation availability or HUD adapter changes.
cases.trigger: At the chosen PauseMenu seam first record a named duplicated decision/dependency eliminated, or retain existing reads. If projecting, mutate returned values and compare owners/another view; cover known/unknown controller observations, covered menu, temporary Workshop return and stale provider. Preserve existing flyability/Continue and crashed-menu-close semantics; expand other status fields only when touched. If nested holds, backend identity or dynamic operation fields are later projected, add their alias/unknown/current-availability cases; the flat subprojection alone does not exercise them.
cases.oracle: No view mutation changes authority or another view. Unknown/unsupported is not ready or false-native; observed armed flags are not new independent admission. Old status cannot authorize a new activity. A flat controller subprojection does not close the entire status/intent contract or retire every callback. Valid other-family bindings remain stored; dispatch/menu closure is not claimed as resumed flight.
cases.evidence: Before/after owner values, detached alias checks, projected reason/support and actual consumer behavior; minimal new fixture is proposed where absent.

cases.title: Replay respects source identity and candidate limits
cases.when: Trajectory, tick input, physics or recording identity may change, or the owning gate requires replay.
cases.trigger: For supported fixed-wing tapes, exact-replay complete baseline on its matching solver/backend. Compare candidate in exact mode if identity genuinely matches; otherwise use supported compatible candidate mode, an owner differential harness or remain blocked. Include mismatch/unsupported-domain negatives. Other families use their actual tape/checkpoint contracts.
cases.oracle: Fixed-wing exact mode retains identity rejection and reports its matching recorded backend; explicit candidate mode reports its actual reference backend. Report mode, completeness, ticks and solver_changed truthfully. Other families meet their own contracts. No identity rewriting, recovered-prefix equivalence, unsupported servo bypass or claim that replay retests raw input.
cases.evidence: Tape/engine/source/backend/config identities and complete CLI or owner-specific harness/checkpoint reports as applicable. Golden helper and short synthetic input tapes do not replace selected flight evidence.

cases.title: Actual native execution is qualified separately
cases.when: Native callback/context/selection/package behavior or native performance claims are affected.
cases.trigger: Run applicable owner parity/fault/refusal/restore tests on the actual qualified native path and matching reference; include absent/mismatched library and unsupported live configuration.
cases.oracle: Requested native or reference fallback does not count as native. Preserve identity/ABI and atomic transaction, fail/reject under the owning admission, and keep package/OS gates separate. Candidate-mode reference replay alone cannot close this case.
cases.evidence: Actual backend/call coverage, engine/toolchain/library/source/data identities and owner-selected full roster; the listed scripts are only entry points.

cases.title: Primary gamepad player flow remains usable
cases.when: The affected UI integration or release claims a gamepad route.
cases.trigger: Run actual setup-to-gameplay UI for each offered action in the selected activity/route and each applicable binding form, distinguishing defaults/explicit overrides, AUX conflicts and fixed fallback controls. Include unique explicit quad throttle_cut and Pause assignments; the throttle-cut offer is a source-derived candidate pending execution.
cases.oracle: Each assignment presented as supported for the current activity has a real consumer and intended visible/command outcome, or is disabled/refused with an explanation. Save/reload or activation preserves its meaning; one event produces the appropriate single action or held/release behavior. Foreign/stale sources do not act. Preserve other-family saved bindings when limiting current-family UI. A gamepad Pause or catalog/validator pass does not certify radio/axis/key forms.
cases.evidence: Activity/route/action/form/context matrix, visible offer, committed profile, actual UI event and consumer, accepted state/feedback and recovery. action-consumers.json contains 37 catalog IDs and five UNRUN examples, with other combinations uncharacterized.

cases.title: Verified radio menus preserve center and command evidence
cases.when: An actually supported verified radio-menu route, proof or shell gate changes.
cases.trigger: After verification, relaunch and exercise the supported menu/flight journey with one radio for both roles. Lose focus/reconnect, then try mouse/keyboard Continue before center evidence; separately test command OFF and the trusted challenge seed.
cases.oracle: Same-radio applicable launch/Continue/restart requires current center evidence even for mouse/keyboard. Radio commands separately require their OFF/rearm policy. Trusted same-generation verification seed remains valid. Throttle never becomes menu navigation; other-role combinations retain their policy.
cases.evidence: Mapping/action proof, source generation, center and command evidence, actual shell gate and supported activity. Radio Pause alone does not qualify radio menus.

cases.title: Device and transport fault cycles match the claim
cases.when: A device/OS/transport is claimed supported or its affected physical recovery is qualified.
cases.trigger: Use each applicable actual hardware-matrix row: idle drift, independent triggers, multiple devices and at least ten disconnect/reconnect cycles, including specified throttle/pause/setup and focus/sleep cases as applicable; test startup ordering and supported USB/BT modes separately.
cases.oracle: No unintended command/auto-resume, correct selected ownership and recoverable holds under the documented family policy. Windows/USB does not qualify another OS/transport. Unavailable hardware or a hung/incomplete run remains unqualified.
cases.evidence: Build/engine/OS/model/firmware/transport/wrapper/profile, actual report/video and outcome per row; unknown metadata stays unknown.

cases.title: Input optimization does not add hidden delay
cases.when: Sampling/buffering/shaping changes or a response/performance improvement is claimed.
cases.trigger: Pin baseline/candidate sources differing by the intended change, match replayable inputs/assets/engine/backend/workload and alternate repeated runs with an unchanged control. Separately follow physical F6 filmed transitions when claimed.
cases.oracle: Preserve sample age/order and first accepted command without unexplained frame queue, invalid-sample masking or behavior drift. Report measured full-workload distributions and uncertainty. Callback counts or replay timing cannot certify physical response.
cases.evidence: Software event/sample/tick/display trace, paired raw measurements/p50/p95/tails/memory; physical F6 has its own at-least-30 filmed transitions and camera resolution, with no promised gain.

cases.title: Lifecycle repetition exposes retained resources
cases.when: Lifecycle resources/listeners change or integration/release soak is claimed.
cases.trigger: Repeat the owner-defined Home/Fly/Workshop/reset/exit workload after warmup with fault/cancel branches; use the applicable global performance or desktop campaign, without conflating their different lengths.
cases.oracle: No unexplained retained-memory/object/listener/worker growth or duplicate event action; pending data follows owner policy. Incomplete soak stays incomplete, and a short finite run cannot establish absence of every leak.
cases.evidence: Declared iteration/time roster, source/host/backend, retained counts and memory over time; device/GPU contention controlled. Existing unit tests are not the soak.

cases.title: Exported controls evidence binds to the actual package
cases.when: Scene/import/UID/backend dependencies move or packaged support is claimed.
cases.trigger: Build the scoped target package with pinned inputs; launch outside editor on its native OS and repeat affected selection/save/restart/focus/recovery routes with required assets and actual backend.
cases.oracle: Packaged resources and identities match the artifact; no editor-only path or missing dynamic asset is silently skipped. Native/reference and physical-device claims match actual execution, with source-only evidence labeled separately.
cases.evidence: Executable/package/source/engine/manifest hashes, OS/backend/device and completed route receipts; existing software delivery tests alone do not certify package playability.

cases.title: Usability and accessibility claims remain truthful
cases.when: Prompts, Controls UI or controller/pilot usability is affected or claimed.
cases.trigger: Follow the owning formative-usability protocol with supported device and EN/ES layouts; inspect accessible names/focus, error recovery, custom remaps and applicable display targets. Distinguish fixed keyboard map from future D6-UX-02.
cases.oracle: No inaccessible action name, disappearing dirty draft or misleading unsupported mapping. Record measured setup/recovery outcomes and user limitations; Mode 1/2 alone does not prove handedness or assistive-device support, and source tests do not establish pilot feel.
cases.evidence: Real UI/participant procedure and observations with device/build/display, existing owner targets and missing accessibility/physical rows explicit.

cases.title: Adversarial transition sequences retain invariant oracles
cases.when: Shared input/lifecycle integration changes enough to create interacting transitions.
cases.trigger: Declare bounded seeds and event/poll/tick schedules combining select/rebind, held input, menu/capture, focus/loss, Save refusal, Continue, replacement and restart on the affected real consumer; record covered transition pairs.
cases.oracle: Assert the selected C01–C24 invariants at each relevant boundary with independent expected outcomes. Preserve a minimized reproducer on failure; generated sequences do not replace required named scenarios or imply coverage of unvisited combinations.
cases.evidence: Actual new/extended harness, seeds, coverage roster, event trace and diagnostics; candidate mutations only in isolated disposable copies if used to prove oracle sensitivity.
